findings.claim: SCN-PIPE-001's dynamic oracle cannot show that a red test run blocks deploy, because the control run it observes is by construction incapable of deploying.
findings.evidence: `pipeline-hardening/4` defines control inputs that "run the real gates and can never publish or deploy", yet SCN-PIPE-001 passes when "the deploy and publish jobs conclude skipped" in that same control run — a result guaranteed regardless of gating. The only static check is "deploy's needs include the tests job", which does not inspect the deploy job's `if:` guard. False result that passes: deploy carries `needs: [tests]` plus `if: always()` (or a separate push-triggered deploy workflow), so a red run still ships on main while every listed pass criterion is satisfied.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a static assertion that the publish and deploy jobs cannot run when the tests job fails (no `if: always()`/`if: !cancelled()`/separate push-path deploy), and/or run the control on a scratch registry/repository where publish is actually attempted and must be blocked.

findings.claim: SCN-PIPE-002's registry oracle is vacuous for the same reason: the vulnerable-image control run can never publish, so "no new tag or digest appears in the registry" passes even if nothing gates publish on the real path.
findings.evidence: SCN-PIPE-002 passes when "the scan step fails, no new tag or digest appears in the registry, and in the latest main run the image-ID step precedes every scan step and the post-scan recheck passed". The first two observations hold for any dispatch control run ("can never publish or deploy" per `pipeline-hardening/4`), and "the post-scan recheck passed" on a clean main run only shows a green recheck, never a blocking one. False result that passes: publish ignores the recheck (`if: always()`) and vulnerable images ship on tag push; the scenario still passes. Nothing exercises the failing-scan-blocks-publish chain the plan's own lesson demands ("no failing scan has ever been shown to stop a release").
findings.suggested_fix: Have the control run attempt publish against a scratch registry and assert it is blocked by the scan/recheck failure, or add a static check that publish's `if:` cannot run when the scan or recheck step fails.

findings.claim: SCN-REG-001 takes its test truth from the system under test and its negative control covers only two of the five task test sets, so vacuous tests would pass.
findings.evidence: "Required test IDs for SCN-REG-001: each of `hosted-small-fixes/1`, `/2`, `hosted-heartbeat/1`, `/2` and `/3` names its new tests in its change's `tasks.md` when done" — the IDs are chosen by the implementer after the tests exist. The negative control only requires that "the required JWKS and setup tests fail against the scratch copies", leaving `hosted-small-fixes/2` (exists() contract), `hosted-heartbeat/2` (running-status rule) and `hosted-heartbeat/3` with no negative control. `hosted-small-fixes/3` is an owner task of SCN-REG-001 but appears in no required-test-ID list at all. False result that passes: tautological tests (e.g., asserting a function returns what it just computed) are named in tasks.md, the suite is green, and the scenario passes while the behaviour is wrong.
findings.suggested_fix: Fix the required test IDs at plan time (or bind them at the cumulative review before any run), and extend the negative control to every required test set, e.g., scratch-revert each change and require exactly its tests to fail.

findings.claim: SCN-LIVE-002's pass criterion compares "the two values" that the plan never defines.
findings.evidence: SCN-LIVE-002: "each of the two values is identical before and after" — no packet section names which two values (training? settings? which fields?), yet `go-live-boundary/2` must write `live-restart.sh` against this oracle. The task author must invent the compared values, and different choices yield different sensitivity to a persistence failure.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the two compared values explicitly (e.g., a trained-model checksum and a settings row) and state where they are read from.

findings.claim: SCN-LIVE-002's negative control passes regardless of whether /data persistence works, so it cannot demonstrate that the harness would detect a broken claim/volume.
findings.evidence: Negative control: "the /tmp marker is absent in the new pod" (`live-restart.sh --check-tmp-marker`). This only proves /tmp is ephemeral; it passes identically if the `sellbird-data` PVC were replaced by an emptyDir again. The control never exercises the failure mode the scenario exists to catch (configuration lost on restart).
findings.suggested_fix: Make the negative control the actual failure mode, e.g., verify the check reports failure when the compared values are seeded from a non-persistent location, or add a step that writes a marker to /data before the restart and requires its absence to be detected as a failure by the same oracle path.

findings.claim: `hosted-heartbeat/2` can require editing `sellbird/main.py`, which the plan assigns to `hosted-heartbeat/1` in the same round, breaking the stated one-file-one-writer rule.
findings.evidence: `hosted-heartbeat/2`: "confirm an idle cycle writes a row and add one if not" with files "sellbird/dashboard.py, sellbird/state.py, tests/**" — but the plan itself locates the write at "`sellbird/state.py` line 2582, called from `sellbird/main.py` line 470", so the "add one if not" fix lands in `sellbird/main.py`, owned by `hosted-heartbeat/1` in the same round 2, while the round rules say "Two writers never share a file inside a round."
findings.suggested_fix: Either list sellbird/main.py explicitly in hosted-heartbeat/2 and sequence it strictly after hosted-heartbeat/1, or move the idle-row write task into hosted-heartbeat/1 so one task owns main.py.

findings.claim: The F1–F3 findings the assess handoff placed in scope are never named or mapped in the plan, so their closure cannot be verified at the cumulative review.
findings.evidence: assess.handoff.json: "Also in scope: migration Job ServiceAccount deadlock, JWKS https rule, DNS policy, F1-F3 and the Trivy control." The plan never contains the strings F1, F2 or F3; its goal 5 lists four unlabeled defects ("the JWKS, exists() and DNS defects" plus the deadlock), so it is impossible to tell which tasks close which F-item or whether one F-item is unaddressed.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a mapping row per F-item (F1/F2/F3 → change/task → scenario) or state explicitly which plan defect each F label corresponds to.

findings.claim: The `none` control run's publish/deploy behaviour is unspecified, so the negative control for SCN-PIPE-001 may push a real image and trigger a real deploy, and can pollute SCN-PIPE-002's registry observation.
findings.evidence: `pipeline-hardening/4` declares only the `failing-test` and `vulnerable-image` inputs as ones that "can never publish or deploy", while operator step 5 approves "the three workflow_dispatch control runs (failing-test, none, vulnerable-image)" and boundary step 11 runs `pipe-control.sh none` before step 12's vulnerable-image scenario whose oracle reads "no new tag or digest appears in the registry". If a `none` run is allowed to publish, it creates real registry state between the two steps and may deploy to the cluster.
findings.suggested_fix: State that every workflow_dispatch control run (including `none`) never publishes or deploys, and pin the registry observation of SCN-PIPE-002 to the specific control run ID.

findings.claim: `hosted-small-fixes/2` leaves the exists() contract undefined for connect failures that carry a sqlstate other than 3D000/42P01.
findings.evidence: "Make exists() return False only for sqlstate 3D000 or 42P01, raise for any connect failure without a sqlstate" — the specified cases are (a) 3D000/42P01 → False, (b) no sqlstate → raise; behaviour for e.g. 28P01 (bad credentials) or 53300 (too many connections) is unstated, so two compliant implementations would differ and the "connect-time missing-database test" would not catch it.
findings.suggested_fix: Specify the remaining case explicitly (e.g., "any other sqlstate raises") and add one test for a non-3D000/42P01 sqlstate.

findings.claim: The goals' live-check items CG-1..3 (domain resolves, TLS serves, Kratos session required) are neither covered by a task or scenario nor deferred in LIMITS OF THIS PLAN.
findings.evidence: goals: "`sellbird.know-me.tools` resolves, serves TLS and requires a Kratos session (CG-1..3)". The plan's live scenarios cover rollout, restart, heartbeat and no-send only, and its limits section does not mention CG-1..3, so the reader cannot tell whether they are out of scope, deferred to the platform phase, or silently dropped.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one line to LIMITS OF THIS PLAN stating where CG-1..3 are verified (platform phase or a later phase) or add a scenario for them.
